product_relevance.what_product_question_it_informs: The size of the publicly reachable web-service surface addressed by IP, as an infrastructure-exposure signal.
product_relevance.weakest_truthful_interpretation: A count of addresses that returned an HTTP response to one exactly specified request. Not sites, not organisations, not adoption of any technology.

proposition.canonical_subject: HTTP response to an IP-addressed GET on TCP/80
proposition.observation_window_semantics: the probe time of the scan that produced the response, selectable before retrieval
proposition.predicate: a request of exactly the form `GET / HTTP/1.1` with the Host header set to the target IP address, sent to TCP port 80, received a syntactically valid HTTP response status line
proposition.inclusion_rule: an address is counted once if at least one qualifying response falls inside W
proposition.exclusion_rule: redirect hops beyond the first response are not separate observations of the population; a virtual host is not an address
proposition.configuration_assumptions: port 80 inside the scanned set for both apparatuses

what_a_positive_observation_establishes: That at that moment that address answered one exactly specified HTTP request.
explicit_non_claims: not the number of websites — virtual hosting means one address may serve many, and an IP-addressed request reaches only the default one
not adoption of any web technology
not a count of companies, users or customers
not comparable with any hostname-addressed measurement

virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.$comment: §6 C2 requires these be evaluated rather than assumed away.
virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.host_header: Fixed into the predicate as the target IP address, because otherwise two apparatuses sending different Host headers are not measuring the same thing.
virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.virtual_hosting: An IP-addressed request reaches the server's default virtual host only. The proposition is therefore about ADDRESSES answering, never about sites.
virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.sni: Out of scope on port 80. A TLS variant would have to fix SNI the same way and is not proposed here.
virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.redirects: The first response is the observation. An apparatus that stores each redirect hop as a separate document must be able to identify the first hop, or its unit is not the same.
virtual_host_and_sni_treatment.why_this_is_the_decisive_issue: It is what turns an apparently easy construct into a same-proposition problem, and it is why one route below is blocked rather than unresolved.

Censys.note: Its web property dataset is described as internet assets responding to hostname-based scans, which is a different population by its own description. The host dataset carries a LAST-observed timestamp, and the dated snapshot's schema is not public.

Netlas.note: On ports 80 and 443 it queries not only by IP address but also by domain names, limits virtual sites per IP to 100,000, and saves each response in a redirect chain as a separate document — and which Host header value it sends is not documented. The population and the unit both differ from an IP-addressed GET, and the request identity that would reconcile them is unpublished.

Rapid7 Project Sonar.note: Its HTTP study documents the exact request — GET / HTTP/1.1 with the Host header set to the IP address — and stores the complete response including headers as a base64 string, in dated files. Documented request identity is what makes this proposition expressible at all, and it is rare.

failed_hard_conditions: at least TWO apparatus routes are PLAUSIBLE
